stem: A client in the third trimester becomes dizzy and nauseated while lying flat during an ultrasound. Which nursing action best addresses the likely positional cause?

options.A: Keep the client supine and elevate the legs to increase venous return without changing trunk position.
options.B: Turn the client onto a side to relieve gravid-uterus compression of major vessels and restore venous return.
options.C: Give a carbohydrate drink before repositioning because late-pregnancy supine dizziness usually reflects hypoglycemia.
options.D: Continue the ultrasound with the client flat for several minutes and reposition if the dizziness fails to resolve spontaneously.

rationale: In later pregnancy, the gravid uterus can compress major vessels when the client lies supine, decreasing venous return and producing dizziness or hypotension. ACOG advises avoiding prolonged back-lying later in pregnancy and turning to either side when found supine. Therefore B directly corrects the likely positional mechanism. A and D leave the provoking position unchanged, and C assumes hypoglycemia without evidence.
educational_objective: Relieve symptomatic supine aortocaval compression in later pregnancy by repositioning the client onto a side.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
source_document_title: Can I sleep on my back when I'm pregnant?; Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period
source_version_date: ACOG current guidance; professional Committee Opinion April 2020 with current live page, patient guidance live as accessed 2026-08-16
source_locator: Ask ACOG ‘Can I sleep on my back when I'm pregnant?’ — second/third trimester back-lying may compress a major blood vessel and cause dizziness; side positioning advised. Committee Opinion ‘Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period’ → Anatomic and Physiologic Aspects of Exercise in Pregnancy — supine position after 20 weeks may decrease venous return due to aortocaval compression and lead to hypotension.
source_claim_supported: Supine positioning later in pregnancy can cause major-vessel/aortocaval compression with reduced venous return and dizziness/hypotension; side positioning relieves the provoking position.

source_original.stem: A client in the third trimester becomes dizzy and nauseated while lying flat during an ultrasound. Which nursing action best addresses the likely cause?

options.A: Keep the client supine and elevate the legs to increase venous return without changing trunk position.
options.B: Turn the client onto a side to relieve gravid-uterus compression of major vessels and restore venous return.
options.C: Give a carbohydrate drink before repositioning because late-pregnancy supine dizziness usually reflects hypoglycemia.
options.D: Continue the ultrasound with the client flat for several minutes and reposition if the dizziness fails to resolve spontaneously.

source_original.rationale: ACOG explains that lying flat in later pregnancy can allow the gravid uterus to compress a major vessel, reducing venous return and causing dizziness; turning to either side relieves the positional compression. Option B directly addresses the likely mechanism. Option A maintains the provoking position. Option C assumes hypoglycemia without evidence and does not first correct the positional cause. Option D delays the needed repositioning while the client remains symptomatic.
source_original.source_detail: ACOG — The Top 6 Pregnancy Questions I Hear From First-Time Moms, sleep-position section: later pregnancy back-lying increases pressure on uterine blood vessels; turn to either side. ACOG expert guidance last reviewed 2026-02; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort; hygiene, comfort, positioning and nonpharmacologic care activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: The clinical key was retained. The stem was tightened to ‘likely positional cause’ to avoid implying all third-trimester dizziness is supine hypotension, and the source package was strengthened with ACOG's professional aortocaval-compression statement plus the explicit side-positioning patient guidance.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Supine aortocaval compression in later pregnancy
audit_findings.source_authority: Official ACOG professional and patient guidance.
audit_findings.currentness: ACOG pages rechecked 2026-08-16; the expert pregnancy page was last reviewed February 2026.
audit_findings.exact_locator: ACOG professional physiology section establishes decreased venous return/hypotension; Ask ACOG establishes dizziness and side positioning.
audit_findings.claim_audit: The final item does not claim every episode of late-pregnancy dizziness is caused by aortocaval compression; it explicitly tests the likely positional cause in a symptomatic supine client.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because it leaves the client in the provoking supine position.
distractor_audit.B: Correct because side positioning addresses gravid-uterus vessel compression.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because hypoglycemia is not established and does not address the positional trigger first.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because it delays correction while the client remains symptomatic and supine.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The immediate positional trigger makes B uniquely corrective; other etiologies can be evaluated if symptoms persist after repositioning.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices are immediate nursing responses with no numeric or wording cue.
audit_findings.blueprint: Fits Basic Care and Comfort through safe maternal positioning.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review checked for overdiagnosis of supine hypotensive syndrome and retained only the supported positional mechanism/action.
